neighbours.label: ' to' in the idiom 'give new meaning to' (preposition completing an abstract relational noun)
fire: The heat wave gave new meaning to the phrase dog days of summer.
His cooking show brings a whole new meaning to fast food.
This tiny apartment gives fresh meaning to the word cozy.
The rainy festival lent new meaning to the term mud bath.
Their marathon meeting gave a new meaning to working late.
The toddler's tantrum added new meaning to the phrase terrible twos.
That traffic jam gave new meaning to the expression standing still.
Her garden gives new meaning to the idea of green living.
quiet: The heat wave gave new energy to the ice cream sellers of summer.
His cooking show brings a whole new audience to the network.
This tiny apartment gives fresh paint to every wall each year.
The rainy festival lent new color to the muddy field.
Their marathon meeting gave a new deadline to the project.
The toddler's tantrum added new stress to the long trip.
That traffic jam gave new delays to the morning commuters.
Her garden gives new shade to the whole patio.
